original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Orthogonal atomic refinement of three distinct target-group spans, with arbitrary Gram-I bases inside shared blocks and complete-plane-compatible grouping.
scope_change_reason: Follow PR3549 different-span handoff. The general hypothesis remains open; restrict to an orthogonal full-block refinement with complete-plane compatibility, proving a new infinite-family tariff obstruction rather than a changed physical coverage law.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper reader tariff could improve paid coverage; the blockwise excess excludes the residual non-Fano route under a precise enlarged contract before native synthesis.
stop_rule: One orthogonal-block proof with exact replays and a focused PR; no general-span search or physical supplier expansion.
evidence: Author-written PROOF.md and RESULT.json; both exact implementations match all 11,856 assignments. Eight actual CLI faults and the complete inherited classification pass registered CPython 3.12 replay. Human/formal acceptance is unclaimed.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

current_deliverable.scope: Orthogonal atomic refinement of three distinct target-group spans, with arbitrary Gram-I bases inside shared blocks and complete-plane-compatible grouping.
hypotheses: Finite binary nondegenerate ambient bilinear space; three distinct indexed positive even target groups, each Gram-I, with disjoint scalar alternating-half target supports.
An orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of the union of the three binary group spans into finite positive even nondegenerate blocks.
Each target group contains either no labels in a block or a complete binary Gram-I basis of that block.
Every paired complete plane stays within its block; bases and plane pairings may differ between groups inside a shared block.
Actual tariff is binary rank of Gram(cl(query),cl(reader)); coefficient field arbitrary; at most four exact additive outer-product terms, arbitrary ambient factors.
current_deliverable.n_definition: nk is total binary dimension of blocks present in exactly k target groups.
